direction.premise: Two tiny, stubborn wizards have no idea how badly their own spell combinations will misbehave, but the duel still reads at a glance.
direction.composition: A bright hand-drawn mossy rune garden in the exact 400×620 duel rectangle, with symmetrical emerald masonry channels, a nested central diamond, two carved double-rune blocks and light worn pavers. The small mages and vivid spell attacks remain high-contrast.
direction.shapeLanguage: Universal Art Forge palette-locked architecture, block-cut square edges, six distinctive small magicians and seven pixel spell forms. No antialiased curved projectile sculptures or ornamental granular stone noise.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Layered ivory limestone and moss pixels, restrained white flowering ivy on the stone perimeter, deeply engraved dark teal channels and crisp square chiseled diamond plaques. Everything is authored in editable Forge pixel rows and code-drawn fixed integer shapes, never an imported scene image.
direction.paletteLogic: Light sage and cream stone provide calm negative space; muted emerald and slate-green geometry emphasize the two raised carved cover blocks; spell bolts and compact fighters contrast without making the environment darker.
direction.typography: Headings use an old-book serif as a restrained signboard; interface text uses sturdy system sans, short Russian instructions and plain names such as Шар больнее.
direction.signature: A bespoke botanical rune court: a central nested stone diamond and cross-channel connects four carved stones, while ivy grows around the perimeter and two raised engraved rune barriers.
direction.distinction: Unlike VENETS parchment political screens and MEAT.EXE first-person corridors, Perekos has an unframed bird's-eye arcade arena with bottom-corner direct spell buttons.

architecture.primaryVerb: Run with one thumb, aim a single class-specific spell with the other, and craft three independent reaction chains between rounds.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Crisp 24px spell silhouettes and confirmed impact frames on a luminous 32px hand-cut limestone courtyard, with two unchanged server-authoritative stone collision barriers dressed in engraved panels and moss.
architecture.spatialRationale: Borderless portrait arena, status on the top edge, left movement and right adjustable thumb aim; a character selector and three inset handwritten spell lanes replace the original single long build list.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The first-person apartment owns the entire frame with a gun overlay, while Perekos uses an overhead stone battleground and explicit two-sided health labels.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Perekos demands two-thumb movement and casting with between-round rune selection instead of room exploration, discovery and first-person gun interaction.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Fog of Conquest frames a discoverable strategic map with units, structures, economy and terrain information, whereas Perekos keeps two large readable pixellated fighter silhouettes directly on an uninterrupted portrait arena with hand-sized tactical thumb controls.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Simultaneous thumb movement and spell casting plus a short between-round build queue differs from Fog of Conquest's deliberate turn-based unit selection, resource use, fog of war and map-scale orders.

comparisons.spatialDifference: MEAT.EXE is a full-screen first-person flesh labyrinth, whereas this title places tiny top-down characters and handmade masonry under a visible light-colored rune sheet.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Holding projectile fire and selecting permanent between-round upgrades replaces first-person weapon aiming, pickups and navigating a procedural maze.

comparisons.spatialDifference: The 5x5 tactical game uses a distinct framed board and its order planning layer; Perekos keeps an unframed real-time moving world behind contextual result sheets.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Real-time dodging, spell cooldowns and hold-to-fire differ from ordered tactical commands and simultaneous phase resolution.

comparisons.spatialDifference: ЧЕПУХА размещает одно письмо на ровной письменной странице, а ПЕРЕКОС заполняет экран движущейся пиксельной каменной ареной и двумя персонажами с портретными значками.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Набор текста и передача скрытых фрагментов ЧЕПУХИ противопоставлены реальному управлению магом, прицеливанию и сборке цепочки рун между дуэлями.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Замазка показывает центральный холст для рисования и компактные инструменты вокруг него; ПЕРЕКОС занимает всю доступную область непрерывным полем боя, а мастерская рун открывается между раундами вместо наложения на само действие.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Замазка опирается на точные штрихи, заливку и голосование за работы, тогда как ПЕРЕКОС — на непрерывное уклонение, направляемые пальцем атаки, выбор персонажа с трейтом и составление трёх независимых цепочек рун.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Cavitation Lab is a fluid-physics instrumentation workspace organized around a tank and measurement readouts. Perekos is a hand-authored portrait dueling courtyard where two tiny wizard silhouettes and their physical spell traces own the frame, with sparse perimeter controls instead of experimental gauges.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Cavitation Lab focuses on adjusting physical parameters and observing fluid behavior. Perekos uses moment-to-moment two-thumb movement, directional casting, hits, and between-round rune chains; the new stone debris is visual feedback for server-confirmed hits, not a physics-simulation UI.

comparisons.spatialDifference: PetriForge gives a laboratory workspace to a large editable experiment grid with sidebar tools, whereas Perekos uses an immersive vertical duel arena with two 24x32 authored pixel combatants and controls on its perimeter.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Training policy agents and moving their goals in PetriForge differs from real-time thumb steering, aiming and arranging spell reaction runes between match rounds.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Shock Lab builds physical bodies, flow sources, pipes and pressure traces in a material-construction canvas; Perekos presents a close-up enclosed fantasy duel court whose light UI exposes only immediate combat choices.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Shock Lab explores material response and boundary conditions through repeatable experiments. Perekos needs fast reactions to enemy spells and rune-driven tactics rather than editing continuous fluid sources and measurement probes.

production.renderer: Quick PWA 400x620 Canvas; real Universal Art Forge 32px court atlas, 24px spell atlas, 24x32 mage atlas, all indexed with source hashes and offline precache. Nearest pixel sampling, no runtime smoothing of geometric sprites.
production.focalAsset: Hand-authored lime-stone and creeping-ivy source frames in Universal Art Forge; the single central nested diamond and symmetrical channels are assembled as pixel-exact logical shapes in forge-court.mjs, not captured from the selected reference PNG.

motion.character: Movement and spells are instant and snappy, while robe and hat gently bob to keep the character alive and distinguish standing still from a frozen sprite.
motion.action: A player touches the fire button while moving and aiming away from the opponent to direct a sequence of small magic bolts.
motion.anticipation: The spell action has intentionally almost no wind-up for responsiveness; the hand-held staff is already posed toward the enemy.
motion.response: The spell appears in the same simulated tick, and a small gold muzzle bloom plus a short synthesized sound makes firing unambiguous.
motion.followThrough: The bolt leaves a short luminous trail and a tiny pixel burst on masonry or the enemy; the shield ring expands briefly before settling.
motion.interruption: Dash, shield and attack inputs are sampled in a fixed update loop; release or new direction cancels ongoing continuous casting without queued commands.
motion.reducedMotion: Reduced-motion mode retains hit blocks, ring outlines, projectile positions and score/health changes without CSS transitions and excess movement.

evidence.expectedChange: In mobile and desktop screenshots, the court should match the selected pale green garden concept (ivory pavers, mossy edge, central vertical/horizontal green rune channels, nested central diamond and two engraved obstacles) rather than the old dark green checker floor. The scene must remain sharp at 400×620 and preserve all controls.
